item.title: Looking forward 2026 | Year of great expectations
item.description: From a politically charged World Cup to high-stakes court cases, party leadership tests and wars searching for an end. 2026 is shaping up to be a year defined by expectation on the pitch, in the courtroom and across Malta’s political landscape

item.title: Finding the will power to change | Sandra Gauci
item.description: The Constitutional Court case, which hopefully will reach some form of conclusion next January could possibly give some indication as to what the future has in store for our electoral system... It has cost us blood and tears to get there but we did and now we are hoping against hope that we get a positive outcome

item.title: The best way to predict the future is to create it | Robert Abela
item.description: 2026 will be a decisive year for our nation. We have achieved much, but this is not the moment to pause

item.title: A letter to the nation | Alex Borg
item.description: May the new year bring us closer to the Malta we know is possible; fairer, kinder, stronger

item.title: Looking forward 2026 | Robert and Alex: From gym vids, to beef and loose ends
item.description: For Robert Abela and Alex Borg, 2026 will prove crucial. Bar any surprises, 2026 will be the run up to the next general election for which we can expect the political heat to start notching up

item.title: The first domino: Why 2026 is Malta’s moment for a real alternative | Mark Camilleri Gambin
item.description: 2026 presents an exciting opportunity for Momentum to guide Malta towards a prosperous and responsible future

item.title: Advancing the arts in 2026
item.description: We hope 2026 can be the launchpad for this vision through a concerted government-wide effort to professionalise the sector across the board through concrete, tangible steps that start addressing the lacunae that exist

item.title: Government and opposition call for democratic, peaceful transition in Venezuela
item.description: Government says it is following situation in Venezuela, while the PN echoes the EU's cautious outlook on the situation, while reminding that Malta had never recognised Nicolas Maduro as the Venezuelan president

item.title: Party leaders share their views on the new year
item.description: Their views also reflect how they see themselves and their parties in relation to Malta's political scene in 2026

item.title: Former European Commissioner, Labour MP say US actions in Venezuela are unacceptable
item.description: PL MP Edward Zammit Lewis stated that Trump’s actions create a dangerous precedent for sovereign but defenceless states like Malta, while former European Commissioner Helena Dalli likened the US actions to the Russian invasion of Ukraine
